title: Quant tuning load harness: INT4 stability vs throughput
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Build an automated load/benchmarking harness focused on aggressive quantization profiles (INT4 primary, INT8 and FP16 as controls) that measures tokens/sec, p95/p99 latency, and quality regressions on a representative prompt set. The harness will be used to evaluate per-layer and per-block quantization strategies, calibration approaches (KL, MSE), and runtime fallback policies. Key goals: obtain throughput curves across sequence length distributions, detect quality regressions automatically, and recommend safe quantization profiles for production serving.
acceptance_criteria: Harness runs end-to-end nightly against the canonical "golden" prompt set and uploads summarized results to the quant-dashboard.
Regression detector raises an alert if semantic-similarity drops >1.5% absolute vs FP16 baseline or if p95 latency increases >10% for a pinned throughput target.
Produce per-model, per-profile CSV artifacts containing tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, memory usage, and quality metrics for FP16/INT8/INT4 runs.
Implementation includes configurable knobs: sequence length mix, batch size distribution, KV-cache warmup, and kernel selection flags; documented in the runbook.
CI job validates that INT4 profile provides >=30% tokens/sec uplift over FP16 on the same hardware for at least 2 model families (Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B) without failing the quality threshold.
PR with implementation and unit/integration tests merged to main and a demo dashboard panel added to the quant-monitoring space.
comments: 2025-02-15 - Miguel Torres: Created ticket. Initial scoping: focus on L2-13B and M7B. Will reuse synthetic trace generator from ENG-41201 and the golden prompt set owned by PM-221.

2025-02-18 - Anika Shah: Prototype test harness running locally. Early runs show INT4 increases tokens/sec but introduced tail-latency spikes under mixed short/long sequence mix. Saving traces and heap profiles to /tmp/quant-runs.

2025-02-21 - Design review: Decided to include a calibration stage (KL divergence + MSE) and compare against per-channel symmetric quantization. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QUANT/INT4+Load+Harness (draft).

2025-02-24 - Bench run (A100-40GB): FP16 baseline (L2-13B) tokens/sec=38,400; INT8=52,100 (+36%); INT4=75,600 (+97%). p95 latencies: FP16=110ms, INT8=86ms, INT4=90ms. Semantic-similarity (embedding-based cosine) drop vs FP16: INT8=0.7%, INT4=2.6% -> exceeds 1.5% threshold for L2-13B.
2025-02-26 - Decision: Add selective per-layer higher-precision retention (first two transformer blocks keep INT8) to reduce quality loss. Re-run scheduled.

2025-03-01 - Run with hybrid profile (top-2 blocks INT8, rest INT4): tokens/sec=69,800; semantic drop=1.1% (within threshold); p95=95ms. Captured PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821
2025-03-03 - Implementation note by infra team (L. Nguyen): Need to expose kernel-selection flag so CI can toggle int4 microkernels. filed ENG-62902 as dependency.

2025-03-04 - Anika Shah: Hooked regression detector into quant-dashboard. Alerting rules created: quality-drop >1.5% or p95 regression >10% triggers PagerDuty for oncall-runtime. Added runbook steps for rollback and canary fallback to INT8.
notes: Use representative prompt mixes: 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512) to mimic production traffic.
Calibration datasets: compare small curated QA set vs sampled production prompts (anonymized) for calibration sensitivity.
Regression detection: use rolling-window baseline (last 7 nightly runs) and require 3 contiguous failing runs before auto-blocking a release candidate.
Fallback policy: automated canary route with 5% traffic to INT4; if alert fires, shift 80% to INT8 while investigations run.
Cost metric: compute estimated $/M tokens for each profile using existing cost model to inform product recommendations.
